== Identification and sources (27 October 2026) ==

* '''Identification:''' the article treats the SWCCG player Curtiss Murphy, the games engineering executive (the professional profile cited in the article) and the namesake of [[Pucumir Thryss]] as one person. This rests on Bill Bisco's judgment (27 October 2026) and the Small World Rule: a distinctive name plus a Norfolk/Virginia Beach games connection.
* '''Evidence:'''
** The 1998 swccg-discussion post #36982 (the [[Curtiss Murphy Ties in the Dark|Ties in the Dark]] deck) is signed "Curtiss Murphy, Senior Software Engineer, Appropriate Technologies, Inc." His 1998 staff page at Appropriate Technologies (Chesapeake, Virginia) calls him a competitive Star Wars CCG player ranked in the top 30.
** The signed-in profile view (read 27 October 2026, not preserved) lists Appropriate Technologies 1994–2000, then EA, Alion (Norfolk) and Double Plus/Gigi Games (Virginia Beach), now MobilityWare; education Virginia Tech. The same employer in the same years ties the profile to the 1998 SWCCG player.
** In ''Game Design Zen'' episode 015 (15 December 2015, 25:29–28:18) he says he was a Decipher playtester and that Pucumir Thryss is the anagram of his name. The show notes say "Star Wars – Pucumir Thryss – Anagram of me!". Audio checked by transcribing the clip (faster-whisper small.en).
** The portrait is the profile's own photo; the signed-out public view serves the same photograph.
* '''Source disagreement:''' in the podcast he places the anagram cards in the Cloud City expansion. [[Pucumir Thryss]] was printed in [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]; its lore mentions Cloud City. The article follows the card.
* '''Missing data:'''
** The signed-out public profile hides the experience list, so EA, Alion, EVMS, netdecisions and Double Plus/Gigi Games are not cited in the article. They need a signed-in snapshot (the login-walled procedure).
** The episode audio file (traffic.libsyn.com GDZ015_SeasonOneFinale.mp3) could not be saved to Wayback (Save Page Now failed, 27 October 2026). The episode is cited through its Apple Podcasts page.
** No Decipher source confirms his playtester account; the fan list gives "????".
